episode_title: Uber for Business's Global Enablement Strategy

real_qa.q: What is Uber for Business and what problems does it solve for enterprises?
real_qa.r: Uber for Business is the enterprise layer that sits on top of the consumer Uber app, helping organizations manage and optimize their mobility and meal spending. It provides a centralized platform for employees' existing personal Uber usage charged to corporate cards, offering easier expense management and giving organizations visibility and controls over how employees spend on the app.

real_qa.q: How has Uber for Business structured its enablement team to balance global consistency with regional market needs?
real_qa.r: Uber for Business implemented a structure combining central enablement and regional enablement. Regional enablement leads sit in-market with sales teams to respond to market-specific needs and nuances, while central enablement focuses on scalable programs like playbooks that work consistently across all regions. They communicate weekly across all regions to share best practices and identify opportunities to scale successful initiatives.

real_qa.q: What are the key success metrics Uber for Business uses to measure AI tool adoption and impact?
real_qa.r: Adoption is the biggest success metric, measuring how sellers are adopting and utilizing new tools. Performance metrics are also critical—they look for upticks in conversion rates or ramp time to indicate whether new tools are moving the needle and helping the business.
real_qa.requete: AI tool adoption success metrics sales

real_qa.q: What is Uber for Business's onboarding approach for new account executives?
real_qa.r: Onboarding is structured as a mix of on-demand learning and a one-week virtual live boot camp conducted via Zoom, followed by manager coaching and additional activities. A key innovation is having BDRs prospect leads before new AEs start their first day, so they arrive with warmed-up leads to accelerate their time to first opportunity and build confidence from day one.
real_qa.requete: sales onboarding boot camp first opportunity

real_qa.q: Why does Uber for Business classify seller recognition and President's Club as part of the enablement function?
real_qa.r: The enablement leader views seller recognition as inherently part of enablement because they see these winners from onboarding through their challenges and successes as AEs, and ultimately celebrate them at their biggest career success when they win President's Club. It creates a unique full-cycle perspective from an enablement standpoint.

guest.bio_context: The guest joined Uber for Business in 2021 as an individual contributor focused on product, systems, and tools enablement. Over approximately four years, they progressed through manager and director roles to become Global Head of Enablement, leading a team that has grown from five people to match the expansion of the go-to-market organization. Their career at Uber for Business has focused on identifying where work matters most and solving the biggest business problems through strategic enablement.

real_quote: The biggest change for me in moving from IC to manager and then now from global lead has been the very conscious practice of stepping away from the tactical work, taking that extra step back to say, is this the work that we should be doing?
